options.B: A receptor fusion protein
options.C: A chimeric monoclonal antibody
options.D: A humanized monoclonal antibody
options.E: A fully human monoclonal antibody

items.why: -ximab marks a chimeric antibody; infliximab is a chimeric anti-TNF-α antibody.

items.label: Practice-exam question
items.stem: Why do corticosteroids suppress a broader range of inflammatory mediators than NSAIDs?

options.A: They act centrally on the hypothalamus
options.B: They block phospholipase A₂, upstream of COX
options.C: They deplete B cells that release prostaglandins
options.D: They block COX-2 more strongly than any NSAID
options.E: They neutralize TNF-α outside the cell

items.why: Corticosteroids block phospholipase A₂, preventing arachidonic acid release, so a broad range of mediators falls; NSAIDs act only at COX.

items.label: Practice-exam question
items.stem: Which drug pairing does the lecture flag for a higher GI ulcer risk?

options.A: Acetaminophen plus N-acetylcysteine
options.B: NSAID plus a corticosteroid
options.C: NSAID plus an ACE inhibitor
options.D: NSAID plus an anticoagulant
options.E: NSAID plus a diuretic

items.why: NSAIDs combined with corticosteroids raise GI ulcer risk.

items.label: Practice-exam question
items.stem: A pharmacist calls: a new prescription reads “methotrexate 15 mg by mouth daily” for RA. What is the safety problem?

options.A: It should be twice daily for steady levels
options.B: Nothing — daily dosing is standard for RA
options.C: It should be IV only in RA
options.D: It needs N-acetylcysteine with each dose
options.E: It should be weekly; daily dosing can be fatal

items.why: Methotrexate is dosed weekly, not daily — a critical patient-safety point, since daily dosing can be fatal.

items.label: Practice-exam question
items.stem: Which sequence describes joint destruction in rheumatoid arthritis, as opposed to osteoarthritis?

options.A: Synovitis forms a pannus; TNF-α and IL-6 drive erosion
options.B: Prostaglandin loss thins the gastric mucosa
options.C: Mechanical wear degrades cartilage; osteophytes form
options.D: NAPQI binds proteins in the synovial lining
options.E: Uric acid crystals deposit and trigger a flare

items.why: RA is autoimmune: immune activation causes synovitis with pannus formation that erodes cartilage and bone, with TNF-α and IL-6 driving inflammation and damage — the cytokines biologics target.

items.label: Practice-exam question
items.stem: Which set lists methotrexate's key adverse effects from the lecture?

options.A: Retinopathy, cardiomyopathy, myopathy
options.B: GI bleeding, AKI, cardiovascular events
options.C: Hepatotoxicity, marrow suppression, pulmonary toxicity
options.D: Tinnitus, aseptic meningitis, rash
options.E: Hypersensitivity, lymphoma, heart failure

items.why: Methotrexate's key adverse effects are hepatotoxicity, bone marrow suppression, and pulmonary toxicity; folate reduces toxicity.

items.label: Practice-exam question

options.B: It lowers GI risk but raises cardiovascular risk
options.C: It raises GI risk but lowers cardiovascular risk
options.D: It has no effect on inflammatory prostaglandins
options.E: It protects the kidney but harms the liver

items.why: COX-2 selectivity gives a lower ulcer/bleeding risk but is associated with more cardiovascular events; renal risk is unchanged.

items.label: Practice-exam question

options.D: Inhibiting dihydrofolate reductase
options.E: Blocking IL-6 receptor signaling

items.why: Rituximab is B-cell targeted therapy: it depletes or modulates B lymphocytes.

items.label: Practice-exam question

options.B: Neuropathic pain
options.C: Phantom pain
options.D: Acute pain
options.E: Chronic pain

items.why: Acute pain has recent onset and is often tied to an identifiable injury or flare.

items.label: Practice-exam question

options.B: Relieving mild-to-moderate pain

options.D: Lowering fever
options.E: Reducing peripheral inflammation

items.label: Practice-exam question
items.src: L03 S41; S41 (notes); S45 (notes); p. 676; p. 701
items.stem: A 45-year-old has symmetric hand-joint swelling, morning stiffness, and a positive rheumatoid factor. Why are NSAIDs alone not enough?

options.A: NSAIDs have no analgesic effect in any arthritis
options.B: NSAIDs are contraindicated in everyone with RA
options.C: RA is degenerative, so only steroid injections work
options.D: RA pain is neuropathic and needs nerve blockers
options.E: RA needs disease-modifying therapy, not pain relief alone

items.why: RA is an autoimmune, systemic inflammatory disease whose goal is to suppress disease activity; NSAIDs ease symptoms without altering the disease course.

options.E: Reassure that OTC products are always safe

items.label: Drug fact
items.text: Tofacitinib: Boxed warning (all JAK inhibitors): VTE (DVT, PE), major cardiovascular events, and cancer; more herpes zoster; ↑ LDL.

items.label: Drug fact
items.text: Tofacitinib: Dose-reduce in moderate hepatic or renal impairment; avoid in severe hepatic disease; caution with diverticulitis.
items.front: Which drug? Dose-reduce in moderate hepatic or renal impairment; avoid in severe hepatic disease; caution with diverticulitis.

items.label: Drug fact
items.text: Tofacitinib: Immunosuppression → infection risk: screen for TB (IGRA or TST) and hepatitis B/C, update vaccines before starting, then CBC and liver/kidney labs every 1–3 months; report fevers promptly.
